first.rationale: The two metrics actually degrading are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and the inherited record points at onboarding friction as the lever with the most direct, repeatedly-observed effect on those exact metrics (memory_86, reinforced by memory_31 for SMB signup). That makes simplify_onboarding the best single-slot bet for sustainable qualified revenue: it repairs the funnel stage that feeds every other motion rather than buying volume. I verify memory_86 because it is the memory I am actually acting on and its stated outcome is a proxy (completion rate, time-to-value, 'early adoption') rather than qualified revenue — I need the source record to see whether the original experiment tracked anything downstream of activation, how long it ran, and whether the shortening removed qualification fields that sales depends on. Removing friction can shift the mix toward accounts that activate but never convert to durable revenue; that downstream value risk is real and unmeasured in the memory as consolidated. I verify memory_73 because promotional pricing is the reflexive answer to a competitor's entry pricing and is the option most likely to be wrong in a way the memory hides: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is a short-horizon acquisition claim with no retention or margin evidence, and matching a price-led competitor tends to import their churn profile and reset price expectations for the existing base. If the source record shows durable revenue rather than a first-period spike, I would reconsider; absent that, I decline it. I do not verify memory_57 or memory_44 because neither addresses the failing stage — referrals amplify an already-leaky funnel, and enterprise sales-assist does not touch SMB activation and cannot be stood up inside one week. memory_91 (activation messaging) is the strongest alternative and I hold it as the next slot: it treats the same symptom one stage later, and if onboarding simplification underperforms it becomes the follow-up. Scale is a standard experiment with a real holdout, not a broad rollout: the memories are generally reliable but were consolidated on proxy metrics from a pre-competitor market, so I instrument not just completion and activation but downstream qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention per cohort, and I will not generalize the result beyond SMB self-serve. If verification shows memory_86's lift never persisted past week one, I fall back to activation_messaging at the same guarded scale.

final.rationale: Verification resolved both questions cleanly and in opposite directions. exp_86 held up past the proxy layer: +13% completion, -2.1 days to value, and crucially +3% 30-day retention — the lift survives into a durable-value metric rather than stopping at a funnel proxy. That is the evidence I needed to act on memory_86 rather than merely inherit it. exp_73 turned out to be the failure mode I suspected: +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue look excellent in isolation, but -12% 30-day retention means the discount cohort does not survive its first renewal, and the source record explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated memory had stripped that warning and kept only the favorable half, which is exactly why promotional_pricing was the reflexive-but-wrong answer to the competitor's entry pricing. Matching them would buy a quarter of vanity acquisition and import their churn. So: simplify_onboarding, standard experiment with a real holdout. It targets the two metrics actually degrading (-4% onboarding completion, -6% activation), repairs the stage that feeds every downstream motion, and is the only candidate with verified retention-positive evidence. I hold residual uncertainty despite the confirmation: exp_86 ran in a pre-competitor market, so its lift may be attenuated now that the price-sensitive segment has an alternative — a smoother funnel does not retain an account that leaves on price. I also flag the standing downstream risk that removing signup fields can shift mix toward accounts that activate but never reach qualified revenue, and exp_86's record does not report pipeline quality. I therefore instrument cohort-level qualified pipeline and 30-day retention alongside completion and activation, and I will not treat a completion lift alone as success. Scope stays SMB self-serve; no broad rollout until the retention signal replicates in current market conditions. memory_91 (activation messaging) remains the next slot as the natural follow-on one stage later. On the competitor: the correct response is not to meet their price but to reach value faster than they do, which is what this experiment tests. memory_44 and memory_57 stay unused — enterprise sales-assist does not touch the failing SMB stage and cannot stand up in a week, and referral incentives would only amplify a leaking funnel.
